title: Dizziness and Fatigue
diagnosis: Duodenal Ulcer with Iron Deficiency Anemia
correct_orders: H. pylori testing (stool antigen / urea breath test / serology)

rationale.Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular: Tachycardia from anemia. Flow murmur possible.
rationale.Physical Exam: Rectal: DRE for melena — rule out GI bleeding.
rationale.Iron studies (ferritin, serum iron, TIBC: Low ferritin, low iron, high TIBC = iron deficiency anemia.
rationale.Occult blood, stool: Positive — chronic GI blood loss from ulcer.
rationale.H. pylori testing (stool antigen / urea: Duodenal ulcers strongly associated with H. pylori. Eradication prevents recurrence.
rationale.PPI (Omeprazole / Pantoprazole): Acid suppression for ulcer healing. 4-8 week course.
rationale.H. pylori eradication (triple/quadruple: Clarithromycin triple therapy or bismuth quadruple if resistance concern.
rationale.EGD before H. pylori testing: EGD reserved for alarm symptoms (weight loss, bleeding, >55yo with new dyspepsia). Test for H. pylori and treat empirically in young patients without alarm symptoms.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with progressive fatigue, dizziness, and dyspnea on exertion. Exam reveals pallor and epigastric tenderness. Labs show iron deficiency anemia. History reveals NSAID use and epigastric pain relieved by food — classic for duodenal ulcer. Duodenal ulcers are more common than gastric ulcers and pain classically improves with meals (food buffers acid). H. pylori testing is essential. Treatment: PPI, H. pylori eradication if positive, discontinue NSAIDs. Iron supplementation for anemia. If alarm symptoms (weight loss, bleeding, early satiety) → endoscopy. Avoid invasive testing in stable patient with classic history.
